items.title: ERC1155 receive-hook reentrancy: no nonReentrant guard on NFTMinterV2 mint path
items.reason: Code-scanner CODE-006 walked CEI and cleared this at HIGH confidence (config.price grown + dispatch(nonReentrant) complete before _mint fires onERC1155Received; re-entry is a fresh fully-paid mint, no broken accounting). BUT a minting contract with an inbound ERC1155 receiver hook and NO reentrancy guard warrants a human second look per Law-1 recall — not dropped to /dev/null. If a future change adds a per-wallet/supply cap checked-before-written, this reopens.
items.disposition: cleared by CODE-006; parked for human confirmation, not promoted to candidate

items.title: Single-step Ownable transferOwnership across 7 contracts (no two-step accept)
items.reason: QA-tier access-control hardening (semgrep use-ownable2step). Owner is trusted (Law 3) and a mistyped owner is a reckless-admin-mistake class (C4 known-invalid), so not promoted to a security candidate — but parked visibly as a QA hardening note for qa-bundler consideration rather than silently filtered.
items.disposition: QA hardening note; qa-bundler to decide inclusion

items.title: Uniboost implements IUniboostPooler signature but does not inherit it (interface-drift footgun)
items.reason: Signatures currently match, so no live bug — code-scanner cleared it. Parked (not dropped) because MultiPooler calls Uniboost via the interface with no compile-time sync guarantee; relevant given this suite's ABI-drift history. A future signature change to either side would break silently. QA/dev footgun.
items.disposition: QA dev-footgun; parked for interface-inheritance hardening

items.reason: Single site; QA type-safety note. Parked (not dropped) specifically because this suite has ABI-drift history (M-04/selector-drift lineage in memory), so a hand-rolled selector+args mismatch would be a plausible future footgun. No current mismatch demonstrated.
items.disposition: QA type-safety note; verify selector+args match target signature
